Uses of Growth Data in Rhode Island

• Growth Data are used primarily for:
o To inform instruction
▪ By using the Growth Model Visualization tool teachers have access to
student growth data, which supplements other available data to
provide a broad, rich understanding of achievement
• First available in SY2011-12 (is this right??)
o Educator Evaluations
▪ For contributing educators in grades 3-7 in Math and Reading,
growth is one element of the evaluation model for teachers and
administrators
▪ Has currently been used for informational purposes only
(SY2012-13)
▪ Will be used for evaluation purposes for SY2013-14
o Accountability
▪ Median SGPs (combined for Math and ELA) are used to classify
schools
▪ Implemented in SY2011-12

Accountability System

Growth is one of 6 components for elementary and middle schools:
• Proficiency: How many students have attained proficiency or better?
• Distinction: How many students have attained distinction?
• Participation: How many students take the state assessments?
• Gap-closing: Is the school serving all students, including those with
disabilities and English Learners?

• Progress: Is the school approaching its 2017 targets?
• Growth (K-8): Are all students making progress?
• Improvement (high schools): Is the school improving annually?
• Graduation (high schools): Is the school reaching its graduation-rate
goals?

Development & Implementation Challenges

• Our challenges:
o Increasing field’s understanding of growth
▪ Of growth in general
▪ How growth applies in the educator evaluation and
accountability systems
• Addressing field’s fairness concerns over those who have growth
versus those who do not in the evaluation model
o Collecting accurate data to link students to educators
▪ Actually collecting and verifying the data
▪ Creating policies around who is a contributing educator and
length of time student must be with teacher to “count”
o Addressing Special Cases
▪ For example, team teachers, long-term substitutes, or
teachers of special populations

Next Steps & Priorities for RI

Given those challenges, RI is focusing on
• Creating additional understanding about growth
• Gathering buy-in from the field around using growth
• Continue to analyze data to inform our decisions around using
growth
o Number and location of cut points for students, teachers
o Attendance (students and teachers)
o Understand reliability of estimates over time
